summary:
Donald Trump used his UN General Assembly speech to defend the US-Israeli war against Iran and warn Tehran to make a deal or face annihilation. The Guardian reported that Iran had offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States took reciprocal steps. The remarks leave the prospect of escalation alongside a possible route to negotiations. Separately, the United States, Denmark and Greenland signed an agreement allowing a larger US military presence on the island, including at least two new bases. The deal is intended to ease tensions over Greenland’s strategic position, though it remains unclear how it changes existing arrangements.

Typhoon Dujuan killed at least four people in Japan and caused landslides, power outages and travel disruption. More than 74,000 people in the Tokyo region remained under evacuation orders as authorities warned of flooding and further landslides. In Sri Lanka, a court convicted 15 men over the 2019 Easter Sunday bombings, while nine were acquitted; the attacks killed hundreds and wounded around 500.

British Columbia sued OpenAI and Sam Altman, alleging the company failed to alert police to concerns about the school shooter’s use of ChatGPT; the province says the attack could have been prevented. A UN human rights investigator said US strikes on boats alleged to carry drugs may violate international law and could be crimes against humanity. The EU removed Russian billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from its sanctions list while extending restrictions on nearly 3,000 others, a move Kyiv opposed. UN experts also held Nicaragua’s government responsible for at least eight deaths in custody since 2018.

headlines.title: Trump threatens Iran with annihilation in UN speech
headlines.summary: Donald Trump defended the US-Israeli war against Iran at the UN General Assembly, warning Tehran to make a deal or face destruction. His remarks raised the prospect of further escalation, while The Guardian reported that Iran had offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US took reciprocal steps.

headlines.title: US, Denmark and Greenland agree to expanded American military presence
headlines.summary: The three parties signed a deal allowing a larger US military presence on Greenland, including at least two new bases. The agreement aims to ease tensions over the strategically located island, though details of how it changes existing arrangements remain unclear.

headlines.title: Typhoon kills at least four in Japan and brings heavy rain
headlines.summary: Typhoon Dujuan caused deaths, landslides, travel disruption and power outages in Japan. More than 74,000 people in the Tokyo region remained under evacuation orders as authorities warned of flooding and further landslides.

headlines.title: Sri Lanka court convicts 15 over 2019 Easter bombings
headlines.summary: A Sri Lankan High Court convicted 15 men accused of direct involvement in the 2019 Easter Sunday attacks, while nine were acquitted. The bombings targeted churches and hotels, killing hundreds and wounding around 500, and the verdict advances a major case over one of the country’s deadliest attacks.

headlines.title: British Columbia sues OpenAI over school shooting
headlines.summary: British Columbia sued OpenAI and Sam Altman, alleging that the company failed to alert police to concerns about the shooter’s use of ChatGPT. The province says the attack could have been prevented, putting the company’s safety practices and responsibility to warn authorities under scrutiny.

headlines.title: UN expert says US strikes on alleged drug boats may be crimes
headlines.summary: A UN human rights investigator said there are reasonable grounds to believe US attacks on boats alleged to carry drugs may violate international law and constitute crimes against humanity. The assessment adds to legal scrutiny of the administration’s lethal operations in the Pacific and Caribbean.

headlines.title: EU removes two Russian billionaires from sanctions list
headlines.summary: The European Union agreed to delist Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman while extending restrictions on nearly 3,000 others. The decision drew criticism from Kyiv, which has argued the bloc should increase pressure on Moscow.

headlines.title: UN report holds Nicaragua government responsible for deaths in custody
headlines.summary: UN experts said Nicaragua’s government was responsible for at least eight deaths in custody since 2018. The report adds to international criticism of the government’s crackdown on dissent and weakening of democratic institutions.
